utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Ms. Merinda Stewart, appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic, appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. This morning's witness is in closed session, but before we do that, I understand there are some preliminary matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are a number of administrative matters. Perhaps can I deal with one that I understand was raised yesterday, and I don't think either side is clear why we have to raise it formally but we are told we do, and that is that the sitting on the 22nd of November, which will be a videolink, should be in the afternoon, not the morning. We got an e-mail about that. I thought Your Honours had dealt with that yesterday, but apparently not. Anyhow, can we formally make that application. It's a joint application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So ordered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, the next matter deals with an exhibit that was tendered by the Defence when Witness ST-197 gave evidence, and was marked for identification on the 19th of October, at page 16225 of the transcript, 2D116. Your Honours may recall that this was a map purporting to show various dispositions of what was described as HVO and -- the ABiH army or the Green Berets, I can't remember, in Kotor Varos, at a particular time in 1992. Two maps were shown to the witness. Only one was sought to be exhibited, marked over -- marked for identification, sorry. And Your Honours may recall that throughout I was asking Mr. Krgovic whether this was a copy of an original map, where it came from, and what it was based. And at page 16224, 1, I said, Is this map a copy produced by Mr. Dragan Mihajlovic in Banja Luka, which is to say the technical production from other documentation or is it a map that was produced at the time in 1992, because that makes a difference. And Mr. Krgovic said, Your Honours, what I learned when I obtained the map or I asked to be given the state of affairs as it was in 1992 since I wasn't able to obtain an original from that time I obtained a copy on the Secretariat for Cooperation with ICTY in Banja Luka, I add in parenthesis, and I was told that this was copy of a map dating back to the period. I then asked to see the original and asked Mr. Krgovic to obtain them and he said it would take a couple of months. Well, Your Honours, we decided that we'd try and shorten matters, so an investigator was sent to this institution on the 4th of November, Mr. Koehler, and he spoke to the director of the institution. He was provided with the maps, regrettably, and I think the reason is I gave my own copy to the witness. Not the particular one that was identified but there were a series of five of them and one of them was put to the witness. And the answer we got as to how these maps are produced is that they were produced by an analytical researcher who was working on a project to publish a book on Kotor Varos. It was not actually finished. The maps were based on research done by this gentleman, Mr. Mirko Markovic. He did not possess original maps from the army but the overlays that were put onto what was an ordinary map of Kotor Varos were put on in 2005. They were produced before a book had been published, which was referred to in evidence. They don't have original maps. They did not ask for access to army maps. And they have never been checked, they have never been, as he put it, verified. They need to be updated, they are drafts, and the dates and the entries on the maps are unverified. Your Honour, in those circumstances, I would ask that any suggestion that in the present state of affairs - in other words, they've nothing to do with 1992, we don't know the information on which they're based, we haven't got a statement from the person who drew them - that they have no status at all even to be marked for identification, that map. So, therefore, I'm asking simply that the marking be removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when I was tendering these maps, I was convinced that they were maps showing the positions of the Muslim and Croatian forces in the -- that period. That is, 1992. After the testimony of the witness mentioned by Ms. Korner, I also sent my investigator out, but not to the director of the centre but to the man who made the maps. My information differs significantly from that information which the OTP's investigator has; namely, that these maps faithfully reflect the situation from 1992. It is my intention to call the author of these maps when I start leading evidence. But I'm not going to use this map before I start -- before the Defence case, nor will I request that the MFI mark be removed. I believe nothing would be gained by doing so. I'm not going to use this map in the examination of witnesses before the beginning of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it seems to me that the -- Mr. Krgovic's assertion that he expects to be in a position to raise the level of reliability, to put it that way, of these so-called maps in his -- at the time his case is opened, and that he doesn't intend to do anything further with them in the interim, would suggest that the Chamber need take no action on your application at this time. In other words, the present position could remain, and I think Mr. Krgovic accepts that he -- if is he not in a position to call a witness who can authenticate these maps, then, for the reasons that you have set out, then they must fall away. Isn't that where we are?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the fact remains that, at present, something has been marked for identification exhibit which has absolutely no basis in law or fact for being so marked. And one of the worrying things - and I have raised this from time to time during the course of this case - is it is incumbent upon counsel, before they try and put in a document through a witness, to check the provenance of that document. And Mr. Krgovic clearly didn't. And our concern is that it -- it will disappear into the great morass of matters which never do get resolved. I hear what Mr. Krgovic says. It is presently his intention to call somebody to deal with that. That may or may not happen. But the upshot is that we have got marked for identification a document which has no basis for being so marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may say ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] hold on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, the Chamber is just wondering what exactly turns on this map. Is it something that is of any major importance to your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this map shows the positions of the Muslim and Croatian forces just before the start of the conflict in Kotor Varos. When I received the map, the information I got was that it reflects the state of affairs as it was in 1992. After the objection of Ms. Korner, I didn't give up and, although the witness who was giving testimony could not confirm the details of that map, I decided not to show the other maps, and this one was marked for identification because the witness was unable to confirm the details. At any rate, though, I, just like Ms. Korner, sent out an investigator to the grounds to check matters once more, and my information differs greatly from that which Ms. Korner got. I verified -- I didn't verify with a man who has second-hand information but directly with the author. But as I said, I do not intend to use it, and if I'm unable to verify the credibility of the map, I will withdraw my application to have the map marked for identification. I know how to act in such a case. But this is of no extreme importance for the Defence case, to return to your original question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. It was exactly to show a way out of this conundrum. In any case, Ms. Korner, for the moment, I think status of a document as being marked for identification means exactly that, that it is somewhere in the middle. It's not in evidence, and if it hasn't been de-MFIed, to use this fantastic new verb, by the end of the trial, it falls away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've actually been -- we've got a three-stage process: One, it doesn't even get marked; two, it gets marked for identification; and three, it gets exhibited. My submission was, but I'm not going to spend any more time on it, that it has absolutely no status whatsoever as any kind of document that should -- it should never have been put, effectively, without Mr. Krgovic having assured himself as to what it was and to be able to explain, when asked, what it was. However, I'm not going to pursue the matter any further. I've made the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. We have your comments on the record and I think we will take no further action on this issue at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, a third matter affects purely the Prosecution, and it's the second or third time I'm returning to this. I hope Your Honours have now got a copy of our calculations as supplied to Ms. Featherstone. We are perfectly prepared to admit that there are greater minds than ours that have been working on this, but from our workings out, we don't need to apply for any further time; that witnesses who remain who come under the old timing, as it were, we still have time to call them within the time that's been added. If we're wrong, then all we ask is whoever has done this study tells us how many hours we're short so that we can make the application for the extra hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's how we understand it as well, Ms. Korner. We're working on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Your Honours, just so that's clear. Your Honours, finally I understand - and we may need to go into private session for this - that Mr. Krgovic wishes to object to some of the evidence that I'm going to lead from the next witness. Your Honour, the adjudicated facts that the witness is going to deal with are --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counsel, before you go ahead, please, would you like us to go in private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we need to go into private session before I hear Mr. Krgovic's objection. Your Honours, it is Adjudicated Fact 193, which was disallowed in whole, and Adjudicated Fact 818, also disallowed in whole.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
